tasks.title: packaging: the Linux x64 platform package and the launcher shim

details.goal: npm i -g sangkar-mcp must install a native binary on Linux x64 with no Bun and no build step, and must refuse every other platform by name instead of failing obscurely.
details.contract:
The first Rust release targets ONE platform: `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`.
`package.json`: keep the name `sangkar-mcp` and the current version; `bin` becomes `{"sangkar": "bin/sangkar.js"}`; `files` becomes `["bin", "agent", "README.md"]`; `optionalDependencies` declares exactly one entry, `sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu`, pinned to the SAME version as the parent; `engines` becomes `{"node": ">=18"}` (the shim only — the server is native); remove every `scripts` entry that invokes bun/tsc/biome/drizzle.
`bin/sangkar.js`: `#!/usr/bin/env node`, CommonJS, no dependencies. It resolves a platform key from `process.platform` + `process.arch` and needs exactly one mapping for now (`linux:x64` -> `sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu`). If the key is not that one, or the package is not installed, it prints ONE stderr line and exits 70, naming: the key it wanted, the single published platform, and the version to pin to stay on the TypeScript build (`sangkar-mcp@<the current beta line>`). Otherwise it `spawnSync`s `<pkg>/bin/sangkar` with `stdio: 'inherit'`, forwarding every argv byte, and exits with the child's code. Forward SIGINT/SIGTERM to the child.
The key table is DATA (one map plus one refusal string) so adding macOS or Windows later is one entry, one `npm/<key>/` directory and one release-matrix row — never a rewrite.
`rust/scripts/package.sh`: `cargo build --release --locked -p sangkar-cli --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `strip`, then lay out `npm/linux-x64-gnu/bin/sangkar` and `npm/linux-x64-gnu/package.json` with `{"name", "version", "os": ["linux"], "cpu": ["x64"], "files": ["bin"], "license": "MIT", "repository"}` consistent with the parent.
`npm/` holds the generated layout, committed as a template for the release workflow (the workflow fills the version).
Verify on this machine only (Linux x64): `node bin/sangkar.js status --repo-root rust/tests/parity/fixtures/polyglot --data-dir <temp>` answers, and moving `node_modules/sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu` aside makes the shim exit 70 with the one-line refusal.
steps: Rewrite package.json (name/version kept, bin, files, ONE optionalDependency, engines, scripts pruned).
Write bin/sangkar.js with the one-entry key table, the refusal line and signal forwarding.
Write rust/scripts/package.sh for the single target and generate npm/linux-x64-gnu/.
Build, run the shim against a fixture, then rename the platform package aside and record the refusal.
details.verify:
`node bin/sangkar.js --help` exits 0 and prints the same usage the native binary prints.
`node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('./package.json').optionalDependencies).join())"` prints exactly `sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu`.
Done when: moving the platform package aside makes the shim exit 70 with one stderr line naming the wanted key, the published platform and the version to pin.

progress.detail:
DONE (one cross-task residue, see RISK 1).

FILES: package.json (rewritten), bin/sangkar.js (new, 0755), rust/scripts/package.sh (new, 0755), npm/linux-x64-gnu/{package.json,bin/sangkar} (generated; binary gitignored), .gitignore (+1 rule).

package.json: bin {"sangkar":"bin/sangkar.js"}; files ["bin","agent","README.md"]; engines {"node":">=18"}; scripts pruned to {"release:beta":"npm publish --tag beta"} (the 12 bun/tsc/biome/drizzle entries removed); optionalDependencies {"sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu":"0.6.0-beta.1"} = parent version exactly; name/version/type/imports/dependencies/devDependencies/publishConfig/repository/homepage/bugs/keywords untouched. `node -e "Object.keys(require('./package.json').optionalDependencies).join()"` -> sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu (exactly one key). npm pack --dry-run would ship LICENSE, README.md, agent/*, bin/sangkar.js, package.json (+bin/sangkar.ts, RISK 2).

SHIM: PLATFORMS = { "linux:x64": "sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu" } (one map, one refusal built from it), TYPESCRIPT_PIN = "0.6.0-beta.1" (beta dist-tag on the registry). Refusal, verbatim, one stderr line, exit 70:
sangkar: no native binary for "linux:x64"; the only published platform is linux x64 (sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu); pin sangkar-mcp@0.6.0-beta.1 to stay on the TypeScript build
Shim is `require`-free at top level on purpose: the parent still says "type":"module" (TASK-064 removes it), so it obtains require via createRequire(fs.realpathSync(process.argv[1])) and parses+runs under BOTH scopes — verified with the field present and removed.

PACKAGE.SH: one target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, `cargo build --release --locked -p sangkar-cli --target ...`, install 0755 + strip into npm/linux-x64-gnu/bin/sangkar, platform package.json generated from the parent's version/license/repository; asserts the parent's optionalDependencies pin equals the version before building.

COMMANDS / RESULTS (this machine, Linux x64, glibc 2.43, node v26.7.0):
- bash rust/scripts/package.sh -> Finished release in 2m 31s; binary 30,747,680 B (29.3 MiB) stripped, 34,023,600 B unstripped.
- node bin/sangkar.js --help -> exit 0; `cmp` vs the native binary's --help: IDENTICAL, 1483 B; first line both: "sangkar <name> [arguments] [global flags] — the name comes first."
- node bin/sangkar.js status --repo-root rust/tests/parity/fixtures/polyglot --data-dir /tmp/shim-check -> "no index at /tmp/shim-check/graph.db yet", exit 0; byte-identical to the native binary on the same dir.
- platform package moved aside -> ./bin/sangkar.js --help: exit 70, 0 bytes stdout, 1 stderr line (the refusal above); restored -> exit 0.
- npm i -g shape (/tmp/ginstall: bin symlink + nested node_modules/sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu) -> --help exit 0, identical bytes; nested package removed -> exit 70 refusal.
- argv: 7 args with spaces/quotes arrive as 7 separate argv entries; child exit 7 -> shim 7; SIGTERM to shim -> child traps it, shim exits 143.
- ~/.bun/bin/bun test: 990 pass / 1 fail (baseline before my edit: 991/0). The only failure is tests/runtime.test.ts "MIN_BUN matches the floor package.json declares": Expected ">=1.4.4", Received undefined — the direct consequence of engines.bun -> engines.node. tests/** is outside this task's ownership and TASK-063 deletes it.

GITIGNORE: added "/npm/*/bin/sangkar" to the root .gitignore (git check-ignore confirms); `git status --untracked-files=all npm/` lists only npm/linux-x64-gnu/package.json, so the layout is committed and the 29 MiB artifact is not.

RISK 1 (needs an owner): the suite cannot stay 991/0 while engines.bun is retired. Fix is one assertion in tests/runtime.test.ts:50 (bun-era invariant) or its deletion with TASK-063. Package-json-only fixes cannot satisfy both.
RISK 2: bin/sangkar.ts still ships inside files:["bin"] and cannot run there (#shared/* targets src/, excluded). TASK-063 deletes it; excluding it would deviate from the contracted files list.
RISK 3: the native binary ignores SIGTERM while serving MCP (reproduced without the shim), so a SIGTERM to the shim neither exits nor orphans — the launcher forwards and waits, as specified. Shutdown policy is the binary's.
RISK 4: package.sh built here on glibc 2.43; release.yml must run it on ubuntu-22.04 (2.35 floor) per TASK-059.

Orchestrator verification, with an npm-install simulation of my own: placed bin/sangkar.js at /tmp/shimtest/bin/ with node_modules/sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu beside it, then `node /tmp/shimtest/bin/sangkar.js --help` -> exit 0 and `cmp` against rust/target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/sangkar --help -> identical, 1483 bytes; `status --repo-root rust/tests/parity/fixtures/polyglot --data-dir <tmp>` -> exit 0 and byte-identical to the native answer apart from the data dir I passed. Refusal path: moved the platform package aside -> exit 70, 0 bytes on stdout, exactly one stderr line: sangkar: no native binary for "linux:x64"; the only published platform is linux x64 (sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu); pin sangkar-mcp@0.6.0-beta.1 to stay on the TypeScript build. package.json read: name and version kept (0.6.0-beta.1), bin -> bin/sangkar.js, files -> [bin, agent, README.md], engines -> {node: >=18}, exactly one optionalDependencies entry pinned to the parent's version, scripts reduced to release:beta (npm publish, not one of the bun/tsc/biome/drizzle entries the contract prunes), imports/devDependencies/dependencies kept because the TypeScript suite resolves #shared/* through them until TASK-063. npm/linux-x64-gnu/{package.json,bin/} generated with os linux / cpu x64 / files [bin], the 30,747,680-byte stripped binary ignored by a new `/npm/*/bin/sangkar` rule (git check-ignore confirms; `git status npm/` shows only the directory to add). package.sh checks the parent's optionalDependencies pin against package.json's version, builds --locked for the one target, installs, strips, and writes the child manifest from the parent. Deviations accepted: the shim uses async `createRequire` + `spawn` instead of a static CJS `spawnSync`, because forwarding SIGINT/SIGTERM needs the child handle before it exits and because a `.js` file must survive `type: module` being removed in TASK-064; the file documents both reasons. Orchestrator fix outside the worker's ownership: tests/runtime.test.ts's engines case now asserts the manifest's `node >= 18` floor and that the Bun floor is no longer a manifest fact (the constants MIN_BUN/RUNTIME_EXIT stay pinned), because TASK-058's contract necessarily falsified the old assertion; the suite is back to 991 pass / 0 fail / 6160 expect across 60 files. Nothing was published, packed, tagged or pushed.

tasks.title: CI and release: one target, artifacts, no npm publish

details.goal: Every push checks formatting, lints and tests on the pinned toolchain; a tag builds the single Linux x64 binary and attaches it, leaving the npm publish to the maintainer (it needs an OTP).
details.contract:
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`: on push/PR — `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` on `ubuntu-latest` with `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.100.0` and a `Swatinem/rust-cache` step. `git` must be available for the diff tests. One job only: a macOS job lands with the macOS release (open question 3 is answered "Linux x64 first"), and adding it later must be an extension of this file, not a rewrite.
`.github/workflows/release.yml`: `workflow_dispatch` plus `push: tags: ['v*']`; ONE target, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, built on `ubuntu-22.04` because that image decides the glibc floor (2.35) — record the floor in a comment and in the release notes; `cargo build --release --locked`; run `rust/scripts/package.sh`; upload the platform package as an artifact; create a GitHub Release on a tag and attach the tarball plus the platform `.tgz`. Do NOT run `npm publish` in CI — the release notes say the maintainer publishes TWO packages by hand in order (the platform package first, then the parent), matching `.agents/skills/build-n-deploy`.
Keep both files minimal: no matrix of Rust versions, no `cargo-audit`, no cache keys that expire silently.
steps: Write ci.yml with the single ubuntu job and the pinned toolchain.
Write release.yml with the one target, the glibc comment and the artifact upload.
Add the step that creates the GitHub Release on a tag.
Add the note that npm publish is manual, in which order, and why the platform package goes first.
details.verify:
`python3 -c "import yaml; [yaml.safe_load(open(p)) for p in ['.github/workflows/ci.yml','.github/workflows/release.yml']]"` parses both files (install-free check).
Done when: the release workflow names exactly one target, records the glibc floor, and contains no `npm publish`.

progress.detail:
Wrote the two workflows; nothing else in .github changed (git status: ?? .github/workflows/ only, FUNDING.yml untouched).

ci.yml (51 lines): one job `linux`, runs-on ubuntu-latest, defaults.run.working-directory=rust so the plain cargo commands work with rust/Cargo.toml (no root manifest); dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master with toolchain: 1.100.0 + components rustfmt,clippy (`@1.100.0` ref does not exist — git ls-remote found none — version stays single-sourced with rust/rust-toolchain.toml); Swatinem/rust-cache@v2 with workspaces: rust -> target; then cargo fmt --check --all, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace. git comes from the checkout (fixtures set their own author/committer identity, so no extra config step). macOS is documented as a second job beside `linux`, not a matrix.

release.yml (165 lines): push tags ['v*'] + workflow_dispatch; ONE target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu named once in env.TARGET; runs-on ubuntu-22.04 -> glibc floor 2.35, stated in the header comment, the job name and the release notes; workflow permissions contents: read, job permissions contents: write only; no NPM_TOKEN/secrets/OTP input anywhere. Steps: shallow checkout (notes are authored with generate_release_notes:false and the version comes from package.json, not git describe) -> toolchain + target -> rust-cache -> version from package.json -> `bash rust/scripts/package.sh` (it is the one build: cargo build --release --locked -p sangkar-cli --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, not repeated) -> assertions: executable exists, ELF magic 7f454c46, e_machine 3e00, highest glibc symbol version <= GLIBC_FLOOR, then prints size and sha256sum -> assemble sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu-<version>.tgz (package/ root with package.json + bin/sangkar, the npm pack layout) and sangkar-<version>-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz -> upload-artifact@v4 (if-no-files-found: error) -> softprops/action-gh-release@v2 under if startsWith(github.ref,'refs/tags/v'), prerelease from contains(ref_name,'-'), so workflow_dispatch never creates a Release.

Verify (run from the project root): python3 yaml.safe_load on both files -> "yaml ok". grep -c "npm publish" .github/workflows/release.yml -> 0 (zero in both files). The manual step is recorded in the release-notes body text under "Publishing is the maintainer's step, not CI's": the two packages in order (platform first, parent second), why the platform goes first (bin/sangkar.js resolves it via require.resolve and exits 70 without it), the OTP reason, --tag beta/latest, and a pointer to .agents/skills/build-n-deploy/SKILL.md §9 — the phrase `npm publish` itself appears nowhere.

Executed the extracted run blocks locally (no cargo here, so not the build): the version step emits version=0.6.0-beta.1; the artifact guard rejects the locally built binary (needs glibc 2.39, above the 2.35 floor) and passes with a matched floor, and the non-ELF, 1-byte and missing-binary branches each exit 1 with their own message; the assemble step reproduces both tarballs, leaves no stale members when a file is planted in a dirty dist/package, and the produced .tgz installs (`npm install --dry-run`), with member paths identical to `npm pack`'s (extra directory entries only).

Not run: cargo fmt/clippy/test and the workflows themselves (no Rust toolchain, no Actions runner in this environment). Residual risk: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master is a floating ref because no 1.100.0 tag exists, so if upstream has no 1.100.0 release both workflows fail at toolchain install; the release job trusts runner-provided node, git, binutils (strip, objdump) and file and installs none of them; a workflow_dispatch started on a tag ref does create a Release by design.

Orchestrator verification: python3 yaml.safe_load parses both files; grep -c "npm publish" .github/workflows/release.yml = 0 (the manual step lives only in the release-notes body text, which names both packages, the platform-first order, the reason (the parent's shim resolves sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu with require.resolve and exits 70 without it), the OTP reason and the beta/latest tag rule); the only env-named target is x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and grep for aarch64 / apple-darwin / windows targets finds none; runs-on is ubuntu-22.04 with the 2.35 glibc floor stated in the header comment, the job name, GLIBC_FLOOR, the notes, and asserted on the binary by reading its highest GLIBC_x.y symbol version and failing when it sorts above 2.35. ci.yml is one ubuntu-latest job with working-directory: rust (the root has no manifest), dtolnay/rust-toolchain with toolchain 1.100.0 + rustfmt/clippy (agreeing with rust/rust-toolchain.toml, which exists and pins the same channel), Swatinem/rust-cache with workspaces: rust -> target, then cargo fmt --check --all, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace; git needs no step because checkout provides it and the fixtures set their own commit identity. scope: .github/FUNDING.yml untouched, no other file changed. Not verified, named: the workflows have never run on a runner; the worker could not run the Rust gates itself (it has no cargo on PATH in its shell — the orchestrator's gates cover that, and no Rust source changed), so the ci.yml command lines rest on this machine's green runs. Two accepted notes: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master is a floating ref because no @1.100.0 tag resolves yet, with the version pinned by the toolchain input and rust-toolchain.toml; and the developer machine's own release binary links glibc 2.39, which is why its guard rehearses as a failure there and will pass on ubuntu-22.04 — that is the floor doing its job, and it is recorded in the release notes.
